one_liner: Ranks every number by the fitted curve's value at the next draw, using a polynomial of degree 4 through 5 smoothed points of the last 52 draws fitted to its record of being drawn or not.
registry_status_reason: Released by package REL-1 (releases and WF-1 design v0.1r1, owner decisions WF1-1 and WF1-2, ratified 31 October 2026). Contract runs on real data need the separate real-development gate.
short_explanation: E_3 looks at each number on its own, as a record of 1 (drawn) or 0 (not drawn) over recent draws. It first smooths the 0/1 record of the last 52 draws with a running average over up to 9 draws, then passes a polynomial of degree 4 exactly through 5 of those smoothed values, placed at Chebyshev nodes so the curve does not swing wildly. It then ranks the numbers by the fitted curve's value at the next draw: its top pick is the highest-ranked numbers and its inverse pick the lowest-ranked, with exact ties settled by the project tie rule (TIE_SHA256_V1). The scores are curve values, not chances, so no probabilities are published. A curve fitted to a short, noisy record is least reliable exactly at its end, which is where this method looks; that is what the experiment measures. It uses only which numbers were drawn, not their order or the dates, and needs 52 earlier draws. If the draws are fair, it is not expected to beat chance.
